title: Ordinary etale open tensor comparison commutes with base change
statement:
Let $C$ be a commutative ring, let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion], let $a:Z'\to Z$ be any morphism, and form $U'=U\times_Z Z'$ with projections $u:U'\to U$ and $j':U'\hookrightarrow Z'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Work on small representatives of the small etale sites in the ordinary unbounded constant-$C$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Use exact inverse images [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], termwise extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], and ordinary derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. For every scheme map $h$, write $t_h:h^*(V\otimes_C^L W)\xrightarrow{\sim}h^*V\otimes_C^Lh^*W$ for the canonical tensor comparison [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], and use the canonical pullback-composition comparisons [lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal]. Put $c_N:u^*j^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^*a^*N$. Let $\beta_E:a^*j_!E\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!u^*E$ be the canonical base-change isomorphism of [sbc-prop-extension-by-zero-and-arbitrary-base-change], in the direction inverse to the sheaf mate [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map], descended termwise. Let $\gamma_{j;E,N}:j_!E\otimes_C^L N\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!(E\otimes_C^Lj^*N)$ be the canonical comparison of [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor]. For arbitrary $E\in D(U_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ and $N\in D(Z_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ set
$$d_{E,N}=j'_!\bigl((1_{u^*E}\otimes c_N)\circ t_u\bigr):j'_!u^*(E\otimes_C^Lj^*N)\longrightarrow j'_!(u^*E\otimes_C^Lj'^*a^*N).$$
Then, with composition read right to left,
$$d_{E,N}\circ\beta_{E\otimes_C^Lj^*N}\circ a^*(\gamma_{j;E,N})
=\gamma_{j';u^*E,a^*N}\circ(\beta_E\otimes1_{a^*N})\circ t_a.$$
This is an equality of morphisms from $a^*(j_!E\otimes_C^LN)$ to $j'_!(u^*E\otimes_C^Lj'^*a^*N)$, natural in $E,N$. No boundedness, constructibility, flatness of $a$, finiteness of $C$, or invertibility of its characteristic is assumed.

proof.text: Use the ordinary constant-$C$ categories and the exact termwise functors in the statement. By [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] each $t_h$ is invertible; [lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal] fixes the canonical comparison $c$. Write $B_E=\beta_E^{-1}:j'_!u^*E\to a^*j_!E$, using [sbc-prop-extension-by-zero-and-arbitrary-base-change] and the mate direction fixed in [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map]. Write $\pi_j(E,N)=\gamma_{j;E,N}^{-1}$ for the canonical open projection map of [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor]. These identifications fix the maps, not merely their isomorphism classes.

The square is Cartesian, so [lem-asd-open-base-change-unit-mate] applies for every $E\in D(U_{\mathrm{et}},C)$. With the same $B$ and $c$ fixed in step 1, it gives $j'^*(B_E)\circ\eta'_{u^*E}=c_{j_!E}\circ u^*(\eta_E)$. This is the first hypothesis of the categorical mate lemma with $F_1=j_!$, $G_1=j^*$, $F_2=j'_!$, $G_2=j'^*$, $P=u^*$, $Q=a^*$, $b=B$, and $\tau=c$. The units here are precisely the termwise-descended open-extension adjunction units specified in the helper.

Let $w=j\circ u=a\circ j'$ and let $\gamma_{v,v'}:(vv')^*\xrightarrow{\sim}v'^*v^*$ be the composition comparisons of [lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal], so $c=\gamma_{a,j'}\circ\gamma_{j,u}^{-1}$. For $X,Y\in D(Z_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ its tensor equation for the pairs $(j,u)$ and $(a,j')$ gives $t_u\circ u^*(t_j)\circ\gamma_{j,u}=(\gamma_{j,u}\otimes\gamma_{j,u})\circ t_w$ and $t_{j'}\circ j'^*(t_a)\circ\gamma_{a,j'}=(\gamma_{a,j'}\otimes\gamma_{a,j'})\circ t_w$. Eliminating $t_w$ gives $j'^*(t_a)\circ c_{X\otimes Y}\circ u^*(t_j^{-1})=t_{j'}^{-1}\circ(1\otimes c_Y)\circ(c_X\otimes1)\circ t_u$. This is the second hypothesis of the categorical mate lemma with $H_1=j^*$, $H_2=j'^*$, the derived tensor products as bifunctors, $\delta_1=t_j^{-1}$, $\delta_2=t_{j'}^{-1}$, $p=t_u$, $q=t_a$ and $\tau=\rho=c$, for all $X,Y$ on $Z$; the calculation uses $X=j_!E$, $Y=N$.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-asd-adjunction-projection-map-mate] with $\mathcal C_1=D(U_{\mathrm{et}},C)$, $\mathcal D_1=D(Z_{\mathrm{et}},C)$, $\mathcal C_2=D(U'_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ and $\mathcal D_2=D(Z'_{\mathrm{et}},C)$, and the data of steps 2-3. Its projection map is the adjoint transpose of $(\eta\otimes1)$ followed by $t_j^{-1}$, hence the canonical forward open projection map $\pi_j=\gamma_j^{-1}$ fixed in step 1: the source's open projection is defined by this transpose, and [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor] specifies its inverse sheaf tensor comparison. The two hypotheses have been supplied for all objects, not only for one component. At $(K,M)=(E,N)$ the lemma gives, putting $R=E\otimes j^*N$,
$$t_a\circ a^*(\pi_j)\circ B_R=(B_E\otimes1_{a^*N})\circ\pi_{j'}\circ d_{E,N}.$$
Indeed the two initial $j'_!$ factors on its right combine by functoriality to $j'_!((1\otimes c_N)\circ t_u)=d_{E,N}$.

Every $B$ and $\pi$ in step 4 is an isomorphism by [sbc-prop-extension-by-zero-and-arbitrary-base-change] and [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor]. Postcompose both sides of that equation by $\gamma_{j'}\circ(\beta_E\otimes1)$ and precompose both sides by $\beta_R\circ a^*(\gamma_j)$. On the left, $a^*(\pi_j)\circ B_R\circ\beta_R\circ a^*(\gamma_j)=1$. On the right, $(\beta_E\otimes1)\circ(B_E\otimes1)=1$ and $\gamma_{j'}\circ\pi_{j'}=1$. The resulting equation is
$$\gamma_{j';u^*E,a^*N}\circ(\beta_E\otimes1_{a^*N})\circ t_a=d_{E,N}\circ\beta_{E\otimes j^*N}\circ a^*(\gamma_{j;E,N}),$$
whose symmetry is exactly the asserted equality. All factors are natural transformations in the displayed variables, as specified in the cited statements, so the equality is natural in $E,N$.
